passages.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: “Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz was a man from Teman.
Eliphaz replied.
Eliphaz spoke to Job.
Eliphaz asked a question.
He asked about a wise man.
He said, “Does a wise man answer with empty words?”
He also said, “Does a wise man fill his belly with the hot east wind?”
passages.original: וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ הֶֽחָכָ֗ם יַעֲנֶ֥ה דַֽעַת־ ר֑וּחַ וִֽימַלֵּ֖א קָדִ֣ים בִּטְנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Should he argue with useless words or speeches that serve no purpose?
passages.sermon:
A wise man should not argue with useless words.
Useless words do not help anyone.
Empty speeches serve no purpose.
A wise man should not use empty speeches.
passages.original: הוֹכֵ֣חַ בְּ֭דָבָר לֹ֣א יִסְכּ֑וֹן וּ֝מִלִּ֗ים לֹא־ יוֹעִ֥יל בָּֽם׃

passages.text: But you even undermine the fear of God and hinder meditation before Him.
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz the Temanite spoke to Job.
Eliphaz accused Job.
Eliphaz said, "You weaken the fear of God."
Eliphaz said, "You reduce prayer before God."
Eliphaz said, "You hinder meditation in God's presence."
passages.original: אַף־ אַ֭תָּה תָּפֵ֣ר יִרְאָ֑ה וְתִגְרַ֥ע שִׂ֝יחָ֗ה לִפְנֵי־ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
passages.sermon: Your sin teaches your mouth what to say.\r\nYou choose to speak with cunning words.\r\nYou use the language of those who deceive.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יְאַלֵּ֣ף עֲוֺנְךָ֣ פִ֑יךָ וְ֝תִבְחַ֗ר לְשׁ֣וֹן עֲרוּמִֽים׃

passages.text: Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.
passages.sermon: Your mouth condemns you.\r\nI do not condemn you.\r\nYour lips testify against you.
passages.original: יַרְשִֽׁיעֲךָ֣ פִ֣יךָ וְלֹא־ אָ֑נִי וּ֝שְׂפָתֶ֗יךָ יַעֲנוּ־ בָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
passages.sermon:
You are a man.
You were not the first man ever born.
You were not brought forth before the hills existed.
You are not older than creation.
You do not have knowledge from before the world began.
passages.original: הֲרִאישׁ֣וֹן אָ֭דָם תִּוָּלֵ֑ד וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְבָע֣וֹת חוֹלָֽלְתָּ׃

passages.text: Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?
passages.sermon:
God holds council with His chosen ones.
You are not part of God’s secret council.
You do not hear God’s private plans.
You do not possess all wisdom.
You do not keep wisdom only for yourself.
passages.original: הַבְס֣וֹד אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּשְׁמָ֑ע וְתִגְרַ֖ע אֵלֶ֣יךָ חָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that is not clear to us?
passages.sermon:
You are a man speaking to Job.
You question Job’s knowledge.
You ask, “What do you know that we do not know?”
You ask, “What do you understand that is not clear to us?”
passages.original: מַה־ יָּ֭דַעְתָּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע תָּ֝בִ֗ין וְֽלֹא־ עִמָּ֥נוּ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side— men much older than your father.
passages.sermon:
The gray-haired men are with us.
The aged men are also with us.
These men are much older than your father.
They have great age and experience.
They support our side.
passages.original: גַּם־ שָׂ֣ב גַּם־ יָשִׁ֣ישׁ בָּ֑נוּ כַּבִּ֖יר מֵאָבִ֣יךָ יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: Are the consolations of God not enough for you, even words spoken gently to you?
passages.sermon: God offers comfort.\r\nGod speaks gentle words to you.\r\nAre these comforts from God not enough for you?
passages.original: הַמְעַ֣ט מִ֭מְּךָ תַּנְחֻמ֣וֹת אֵ֑ל וְ֝דָבָ֗ר לָאַ֥ט עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash, as you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?
passages.sermon:
Your heart has carried you away.
Your eyes flash with anger.
You have turned your spirit against God.
You have spoken these words from your mouth.
passages.original: מַה־ יִּקָּחֲךָ֥ לִבֶּ֑ךָ וּֽמַה־ יִּרְזְמ֥וּן עֵינֶֽיךָ׃ כִּֽי־ תָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־ אֵ֣ל רוּחֶ֑ךָ וְהֹצֵ֖אתָ מִפִּ֣יךָ מִלִּֽין׃

passages.text: What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
passages.sermon:
Man is a human being.
Man is born from a woman.
Man cannot make himself pure.
Man cannot make himself righteous.
No person can claim perfect purity.
No one born of a woman can claim perfect righteousness.
passages.original: מָֽה־ אֱנ֥וֹשׁ כִּֽי־ יִזְכֶּ֑ה וְכִֽי־ יִ֝צְדַּ֗ק יְל֣וּד אִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: If God puts no trust in His holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in His eyes, how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?
passages.sermon:
God does not put His trust in His holy ones.
Even the heavens are not pure in God's eyes.
Man is vile.
Man is corrupt.
Man drinks injustice like water.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן בִּקְדֹשׁוֹ לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וְ֝שָׁמַ֗יִם לֹא־ זַכּ֥וּ בְעֵינָֽיו׃ אַ֭ף כִּֽי־ נִתְעָ֥ב וְֽנֶאֱלָ֑ח אִישׁ־ שֹׁתֶ֖ה כַמַּ֣יִם עַוְלָֽה׃

passages.text: Listen to me and I will inform you. I will describe what I have seen, what was declared by wise men and was not concealed from their fathers, to whom alone the land was given when no foreigner passed among them.
passages.sermon:
I am speaking to you now.
Listen to me.
I will tell you what I have seen.
Wise men have declared these things.
Their fathers did not hide these things from them.
God gave the land only to these people.
No foreigner lived among them.
passages.original: אֲחַוְךָ֥ שְֽׁמַֽע־ לִ֑י וְזֶֽה־ חָ֝זִ֗יתִי וַאֲסַפֵּֽרָה׃ אֲשֶׁר־ חֲכָמִ֥ים יַגִּ֑ידוּ וְלֹ֥א כִֽ֝חֲד֗וּ מֵאֲבוֹתָֽם׃ לָהֶ֣ם לְ֭בַדָּם נִתְּנָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלֹא־ עָ֖בַר זָ֣ר בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: A wicked man writhes in pain all his days; only a few years are reserved for the ruthless.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man suffers every day.
He feels pain throughout his life.
A ruthless man receives only a few years.
His time is short.
passages.original: כָּל־ יְמֵ֣י רָ֭שָׁע ה֣וּא מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל וּמִסְפַּ֥ר שָׁ֝נִ֗ים נִצְפְּנ֥וּ לֶעָרִֽיץ׃

passages.text: Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
passages.sermon: A wicked man hears sounds of terror in his ears.\r\nHe feels afraid even when he is safe.\r\nWhen he prospers, a destroyer attacks him.
passages.original: קוֹל־ פְּחָדִ֥ים בְּאָזְנָ֑יו בַּ֝שָּׁל֗וֹם שׁוֹדֵ֥ד יְבוֹאֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: He despairs of his return from darkness; he is marked for the sword.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man lives in darkness.
He does not believe he will return from darkness.
He has no hope for escape.
He is marked for the sword.
He faces death.
passages.original: לֹא־ יַאֲמִ֣ין שׁ֭וּב מִנִּי־ חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וְצָפוּ ה֣וּא אֱלֵי־ חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: He wanders about as food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.
passages.sermon:
This man is wicked.
He wanders in search of bread.
He cannot find food.
He knows trouble is near.
He understands the day of darkness is coming.
He realizes disaster is ready for him.
passages.original: נֹ֘דֵ֤ד ה֣וּא לַלֶּ֣חֶם אַיֵּ֑ה יָדַ֓ע׀ כִּֽי־ נָכ֖וֹן בְּיָד֣וֹ יֽוֹם־ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

passages.text: Distress and anguish terrify him, overwhelming him like a king poised to attack.
passages.sermon:
Distress terrifies him.
Anguish terrifies him.
Distress and anguish overwhelm him.
They come against him like a king ready to attack.
passages.original: יְֽ֭בַעֲתֻהוּ צַ֣ר וּמְצוּקָ֑ה תִּ֝תְקְפֵ֗הוּ כְּמֶ֤לֶךְ׀ עָתִ֬יד לַכִּידֽוֹר׃

passages.text: For he has stretched out his hand against God and has vaunted himself against the Almighty, rushing headlong at Him with a thick, studded shield.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man opposes God.
He lifts his hand against God.
He acts proudly against the Almighty.
He runs at God with his neck held high.
He charges forward with a thick, studded shield.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ נָטָ֣ה אֶל־ אֵ֣ל יָד֑וֹ וְאֶל־ שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יִתְגַּבָּֽר׃ יָר֣וּץ אֵלָ֣יו בְּצַוָּ֑אר בַּ֝עֲבִ֗י גַּבֵּ֥י מָֽגִנָּֽיו׃

passages.text: Though his face is covered with fat and his waistline bulges with flesh, he will dwell in ruined cities, in abandoned houses destined to become rubble.
passages.sermon:
This man is proud and prosperous.
His face is covered with fat.
His waistline bulges with flesh.
He lives in comfort and plenty.
But he will dwell in ruined cities.
He will live in abandoned houses.
No one will live in those houses.
Those houses are destined to become rubble.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ כִסָּ֣ה פָנָ֣יו בְּחֶלְבּ֑וֹ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ פִּימָ֣ה עֲלֵי־ כָֽסֶל׃ וַיִּשְׁכּ֤וֹן׀ עָ֘רִ֤ים נִכְחָד֗וֹת בָּ֭תִּים לֹא־ יֵ֣שְׁבוּ לָ֑מוֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הִתְעַתְּד֣וּ לְגַלִּֽים׃

passages.text: He will no longer be rich; his wealth will not endure. His possessions will not overspread the land.
passages.sermon:
This man once had wealth.
He will not be rich anymore.
His wealth will not last.
His possessions will not spread across the land.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יֶ֭עְשַׁר וְלֹא־ יָק֣וּם חֵיל֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־ יִטֶּ֖ה לָאָ֣רֶץ מִנְלָֽם׃

passages.text: He will not escape from the darkness; the flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.
passages.sermon:
This man is wicked.
He will not escape from darkness.
A flame will dry up his shoots.
The breath of God's mouth will carry him away.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יָס֨וּר׀ מִנִּי־ חֹ֗שֶׁךְ יֹֽ֭נַקְתּוֹ תְּיַבֵּ֣שׁ שַׁלְהָ֑בֶת וְ֝יָס֗וּר בְּר֣וּחַ פִּֽיו׃

passages.text: Let him not deceive himself with trust in emptiness, for emptiness will be his reward.
passages.sermon: A wicked man should not trust in worthless things.\r\nHe should not deceive himself.\r\nIf he trusts in emptiness, he will receive emptiness as his reward.
passages.original: אַל־ יַאֲמֵ֣ן בַּשּׁוֹ נִתְעָ֑ה כִּי־ שָׁ֝֗וְא תִּהְיֶ֥ה תְמוּרָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not flourish.
passages.sermon:
God judges the wicked.
He repays them before their time is complete.
Their punishment comes early.
Their branch does not flourish.
They do not prosper or grow strong.
passages.original: בְּֽלֹא־ י֭וֹמוֹ תִּמָּלֵ֑א וְ֝כִפָּת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רַעֲנָֽנָה׃

passages.text: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.
passages.sermon: A wicked person will lose everything before it is ready.\r\nHe will be like a vine that people strip of its unripe grapes.\r\nHe will be like an olive tree that drops its blossoms before fruit can grow.
passages.original: יַחְמֹ֣ס כַּגֶּ֣פֶן בִּסְר֑וֹ וְיַשְׁלֵ֥ךְ כַּ֝זַּ֗יִת נִצָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
passages.sermon: The company of the godless will be barren.\r\nFire will consume the tents of bribery.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עֲדַ֣ת חָנֵ֣ף גַּלְמ֑וּד וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ אָכְלָ֥ה אָֽהֳלֵי־ שֹֽׁחַד׃

passages.text: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb is pregnant with deceit.”
passages.sermon:
The wicked people plan to do wrong.
They give birth to evil actions.
Their hearts are full of deceit.
They prepare lies within themselves.
passages.original: הָרֹ֣ה עָ֭מָל וְיָ֣לֹד אָ֑וֶן וּ֝בִטְנָ֗ם תָּכִ֥ין מִרְמָֽה׃ס
